Lessons.Title: Compare and Describe Angles
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will consider ways to compare angles and describe the size of angles.
In previous lessons, you identified and described lines, line segments, rays, and angles in geometric and real-world contexts. The purpose of the exploratory work in this lesson is for you to make sense of which attributes define an angle (rays at a common endpoint) and which attributes do not (length of the line segments). The activities in the lesson intentionally elicit your ideas for how to describe an angle’s size.

2021 lesson activities: Warm-up: Which One Doesn’t Belong: Angles (10 minutes); Activity 1: Card Sort: Angles (20 minutes); Activity 2: Order Angles (15 minutes); Cool-down: Compare Two Angles (5 minutes)
Corrected mathematical focus: Compare angle openings or turns, not the lengths of rays; a larger turn means a larger angle.

Edulytics authored guidance: Use source cards to sort angles into meaningful groups. Order the cards from smallest turn to largest turn and justify your reasoning. For quantitative comparison, 115° exceeds 40° by 75°.
First-party Cool-down (not publisher assessment): Which is larger, 40° or 115°, and by how much?
Images, drawing/protractor accuracy, partner tasks and the gated original publisher Cool-down require original task evidence and teacher/visual review.
